name: La Ligne
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $195 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Striped sweaters, knitwear, shirts, pants and denim for women, the Marin sweater at $350 and coats from about $700, sold through its own stores and site.
origin: Founded in 2016 by Valerie Macaulay; Meredith Melling; Molly Howard.

quote.q: If you can’t eat, dance, sleep and drink in it, we won’t make it.

opview: “If you can’t eat, dance, sleep and drink in it, we won’t make it.” — La Ligne (house), Behind the Label, lalignenyc.com

facts_read.source: brand site; FashionNetwork (undated, How the trunk show built La Ligne); nordstrom.com; Vinted brand page; TRR designer directory; B Lab directory; GOTS database

price_read.sublines: La Ligne women's ready-to-wear; EXCLUDED: kids/Mini (tag kids), collaborations (e.g. Observed By Us x La Ligne slippers), sleepwear, accessories

doors.note: 10 locations listed; Dallas Highland Park Village temporarily closed as of Oct 1 (row closed, not counted; no street/ZIP published). 9 open own doors.

craft_evidence.madein: 4 of 79 sampled product pages (5%) state 'Made in New York City'; the rest state no country
craft_evidence.heritage: vague — founders named (Valerie Macaulay, Meredith Melling, Molly Howard), no founding date or place on the page
craft_evidence.reasoning: The brand page is about the founders and the stripe; it names no factory, mill or date. Four of 79 sampled pages say 'Made in New York City' — a real claim on a handful of tailored pieces, not enough to lift the whole range above nothing checkable.
